# Deck-Clearing — Dedup Evidence & Corrected Consolidation Plan

*Generated by `build/find-dup-rows.py` (read-only). This is the evidence batch for the propose-and-wait
consolidation decisions. **Headline: the recontext scan's "merge for free" claims were over-stated — the
data only supports a few of them.** This vindicates the "revisit everything by hand" instinct; most of the
proposed merges are real craft judgment calls, not mechanical dedup.*

## A. Cross-table overlap — what the data actually shows

Measured: for each proposed merge, the % of the thin table's rows whose *concept* (label cell) already has
a near-duplicate (≥0.55 similarity) in the rich sibling.

| Proposed merge (sweep plan B1) | Overlap | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `npc-temperament` → `npc-demeanor` | **0%** | ❌ **NOT a duplicate.** Temperament = adjective labels ("Suspicious", "Patient"); Demeanor = concrete cues. Related theme, different content. Merging loses the temperament axis. **Craft call, not a free merge.** |
| `npc-behavioral-detail` → `npc-mannerisms`/`quirk` | **5%** | ❌ The scan claimed "~17/20 pure duplication" — **false.** These are behavioral *categories* ("Repeated Gesture", "Speech Pattern"), not the d100s' concrete tics. |
| `npc-immediate-mood` → `npc-demeanor` | **5%** | ❌ Distinct (transient mood vs. standing demeanor). |
| `npc-under-pressure` → `npc-demeanor`/`mannerisms` | **5%** | ❌ Bare stress verbs ("Withdraws", "Freezes") — a distinct *vector* axis, not dup content. |
| `npc-resource-control` → `npc-leverage` | **37%** | ⚠️ **Partial.** 63 of 100 rows unique. The "fold tangibles into Leverage" idea has some basis but is a real authoring merge, not a delete. |
| `monster-meal-viability` → `cuisine-effects` | **11%** | ⚠️ Complementary *axes* (is-it-edible vs. what-it-does), confirmed. Merge = combine axes (authoring), not dedup. |
| `dungeon-secret-type` → `dungeon-secret-tier` | 0%* | ⚠️ *Measurement artifact (different phrasing). Validation agent says Tier is a conceptual superset — **needs a manual eyeball**, not a text metric. |
| `urban-scene` → `urban-sensory` | **55%** | ✅ **Real overlap.** Over half already covered — fold the 9 unique beats, retire. The one clean merge. |

**Takeaway:** of 8 proposed consolidations, only **1 is a clean fold** (urban-scene), **2 are real authoring
merges** (resource-control, meal-viability), **1 needs a manual check** (secret-type), and **4 are NOT
duplicates at all** — the NPC mood/temperament/behavioral/pressure cluster is genuine distinct content that
the craft pass should *improve in place or consciously unify*, not silently delete. Adam reviews each.

## B. Internal duplication — split intentional weighting from copy-paste filler

The map's "DUPED" flag (low distinct%) conflates **two very different things**. Do NOT collapse the first group.

**Intentional probability-weighting — KEEP (a repeated row = a fatter slice of the die):**
- `npc-race-weighted` (19%) — *"weighted"* is in the name; the repeats ARE the demographic weighting.
- `dungeon-loot-junk` d300 (14%) — the deliberate Easter-egg/weighted junk table (prep doc: do not touch).
- `dungeon-loot-minor-resource` (43%) — potion-of-healing ×25 = intentional commonness.
- `dungeon-encounter-type` / `wilderness-encounter-type` / `travel-event-type` — dispatchers; weighted categories.
- `npc-role` (38%), `npc-influence-weight` (30%) — weighted distributions.

**Genuine copy-paste filler — COLLAPSE candidates (identical text with no weighting intent):**
- `urban-lighting` d50 → **9 distinct**, "Minor Variation" strings repeated 8–15× as pure filler. The worst
  offender; collapse to a weighted d12 with real per-row variation (voice_critical).
- `travel-biome` d100 → **12 biomes ×~20**, identical strings. The weighting is fine but it's a fake-d100
  that can never throw a fresh fragment → weighted d12, or give each numbered row a micro-variation.
- `travel-destination-type` d100 → **10 types**, same shape — dispatcher masquerading as a d100.
- `d100-urban-general-features` (56%) — borderline; eyeball.

## C. What this changes in the plan

- The "consolidation retires ~11 items for near-zero prose" claim in `REAUTHORING-SWEEP-PLAN.md` §B1 is **too
  optimistic.** Realistically: ~1 clean fold + a few authoring-merges + the rest are craft-pass tables. The
  net worklist shrink from consolidation is smaller than the scan projected.
- The genuine mechanical wins are the **copy-paste collapses** (urban-lighting, travel-biome,
  travel-destination-type) — structural, unambiguous, and they don't touch your weighted tables.
- Everything else flows into the **per-table craft pass**, where you decide unify-vs-improve-in-place with
  the row content in front of you. (This is why the by-hand pass matters — the metric can't make these calls.)

## D. Creature IP cluster — full scope (`build/scan-creature-ip.py`, read-only)

**592 hits · 58 files · all 23 terms present** — bigger than the sweep plan's ~22-file estimate. The scrub
splits into **two kinds of edit**, which the plan conflated:

**(1) Clean token-swaps — the TABLE files** (a creature name sits in a row; swap the noun, prose survives):
- `Dungeon/Urban Threat Identity (+T2)` (30/30/24), `Dungeon Enemy Category` (19), `Wilderness Contact` (30),
  `Wilderness Art` (16), `Place-Secret` (20), `Dungeon/Urban Contact` (13/10). These are the genuine scripted-
  swap targets — exactly like the executed places/factions Phase-2 scrub.

**(2) Real prose rewrites — the MONSTER STAT FILES** (the file is *about* that creature, name throughout):
- `Slaad.md` (41), `Nothic.md` (40, also cross-refs Mind Flayer + Intellect Devourer), `Aboleth.md` (25),
  `Kuo-toa.md` (22), `Grimlock.md` (21), `Flumph.md` (21), `Death Tyrant.md` (18), `Beholder.md` (17),
  `Githzerai.md` (17), `Mind Flayer.md` (15), `Modron.md` (14), `Githyanki.md` (15), `Intellect Devourer.md`
  (9), `Quaggoths.md` (9). Each needs the name genericized *throughout its lore* + a file/`id` rename — a
  per-file rewrite, not a one-line swap. **This is where the scrub is real work, and where it overlaps the
  monster-flavor craft pass (Track D) — do them together per creature.**

**(3) Campaign/encounter content — judgment, maybe archive not scrub:**
- `Asset Library/Adventures/The Hungering Stone.md` (10, Drow/Flumph) — the genericization scan already
  flags Hungering Stone as campaign-bound (exclude/archive, don't genericize).
- `Asset Library/Encounter Modules/Urban/.../The Watcher's Gate.md` (17, Flumph) — a built encounter; decide
  scrub-vs-rebuild.

**Refinements to the plan's B2:**
- It's **58 files, not ~22**, and ~14 of them are stat-file rewrites (not swaps). The "one scripted pass
  retires the cluster" framing holds for the **table files**; the **stat files fold into Track D** (the
  per-monster additive/archive-first pass) so the rename + genericize + new flavor tables happen in one edit.
- `Mechanus` (1) / `Limbo` (1) are nearly absent — trivial.
- `Drow`/`Tiefling` in NPC name tables = section labels only (relabel, keep the name bank).

**Bottom line for approval:** the mapping (term→generic) is ready for your sign-off; the *table-file* swap can
run as one scripted pass on your OK; the *stat-file* genericization should ride with the monster-flavor pass,
creature by creature.
